summary.headline: DCM Shriram Q2 FY27 net revenue rose 22% YoY to Rs 3,977 crore, but PBDIT fell to Rs 319 crore from Rs 408 crore on chemicals input costs.
summary.overview: Net revenue, net of excise duty, grew 22% YoY to Rs 3,977 crore, driven by Chemicals, Vinyl, Fertilizer and Fenesta. PBDIT declined to Rs 319 crore from Rs 408 crore, as higher chemicals input costs and weaker Agri-input earnings outweighed better realisations, and the prior-year quarter included one-time incentives of Rs 76 crore (Gujarat) and Rs 15.5 crore (sugar power tariff). Vinyl PBDIT rose sharply to Rs 51 crore from Rs 12 crore, while Bioseed posted a Rs 41 crore loss. Management declared a 200% interim dividend (Rs 62.38 crore) and flagged a demerger targeted for Q1 FY28 board consideration.

segments.name: Chemicals
segments.commentary: Revenue up 47% YoY with caustic volumes +2% and ECU prices +6%, but PBDIT fell to Rs 158 crore from Rs 254 crore. Production costs rose about 6-8% across chemistries while selling prices fell about 4-6%; hydrogen peroxide was the exception. Caustic utilisation was 88% vs 79-80% a year ago.

segments.name: Vinyl
segments.commentary: Revenue +20% YoY; PVC volumes +29% and prices +25%, Carbide volumes +15% and prices +16%. PBDIT Rs 51 crore vs Rs 12 crore; PBDIT margin about 21.9%.

segments.name: Sugar & Ethanol
segments.commentary: Revenue +10% YoY; domestic sugar prices +14%, volumes -6%, ethanol volumes +24% on timing. PBDIT Rs 62 crore vs Rs 33 crore, with prior-year Rs 15.5 crore one-time power tariff benefit.

segments.name: Fenesta Building Systems
segments.commentary: Revenue +22% YoY with project vertical leading; PBDIT Rs 49 crore (+15%) with margins slightly lower on product mix, input costs and new platform fixed costs. Project business about 45% of revenue.

segments.name: Shriram Farm Solutions
segments.commentary: Revenue -10% YoY on lower Seed and Specialty Plant Nutrition volumes, partly from timing of research wheat seed sales; PBDIT Rs 78 crore vs Rs 106 crore. Crop Protection grew healthily.

segments.name: Fertilizer
segments.commentary: Revenue +40% YoY on realisations +46% from higher gas prices; PBDIT +25% to Rs 25 crore. Outstanding subsidy Rs 446 crore vs Rs 187 crore a year ago.

segments.name: Bioseed
segments.commentary: Revenue lower for quarter and half on weak Kharif acreage; PBDIT negative Rs 41 crore vs negative Rs 7 crore, including provisions for doubtful debts in India (about Rs 7-8 crore) and Philippines seed discard (about Rs 12 crore in H1).

guidance_outlook: Demerger: management targeting a board-level scheme soon and implementation around Q1 FY28.
Shriram Farm Solutions: part of the topline timing shortfall may reverse in Q3 FY27, subject to crop conditions.
PVC: current prices Rs 95,000-1 lakh per tonne; demand expected to improve in Q3 and Q4 after monsoon; MIP of USD 766/MT plus import duty seen keeping prices stable.
Chemicals: incremental depreciation minimal for rest of FY27 (Rs 10 crore in Q2) as most projects capitalised.
Sugar: crushing to start first week of November; cane availability expected to be lower due to drought in Maharashtra and Karnataka; visibility in 2-3 months.
Urea subsidy requirement could reach Rs 1.2 lakh crore vs Union budget Rs 85,000 crore.
Renewable share targeted at about one-third of power requirement within next one year; 70-80 MW more planned; investments return above 20-25%.
capex_capacity: Commissioned 100 TPD Aluminium Chloride plant at Bharuch, taking total to 250 TPD; Calcium Chloride partially commissioned at 133 of 266 TPD.
Commissioned 68 MW hybrid renewable power project at Kota; 58 MW hybrid project at Bharuch on schedule.

New projects: 40 MW peak solar plant at Kota (Rs 145 crore), filter presses at Kota cement (Rs 60 crore), debottlenecking at Bharuch and Kota plus caustic capacity increase (Rs 120 crore), and Shriram Teknor JV lines (Rs 133 crore total, up to Rs 50 crore equity).
Fenesta aluminium extrusion plant at Kota phase one commissioned; phase two in installation; wooden doors facility on schedule.
Chlor-alkali captive chlorine consumption expected to reach about 45% at Bharuch and 62% at Kota after projects; with pipeline customers about 70% integrated.
Management says about Rs 4,500 crore invested over last 3-4 years, with pipeline still available.
demand_pricing: Caustic prices corrected in line with global markets; chlorine realisations improved from about negative Rs 8,000 (Q1, as stated) to about negative Rs 5,000 in Q2, offsetting caustic decline.
Hydrogen peroxide prices firmer as gas costs rose; in-house hydrogen insulated margins.
Advanced Materials: sharp price swings led to high-cost inventory liquidation and deferred customer demand; pressures now largely stabilised.
Global sugar deficit estimated at about 2.6 million MT for 2026-27; domestic sugar price around Rs 4,800 per quintal, expected range-bound.

Ethanol: 2026-27 tender restricted to C-heavy and grain feedstock; maize ethanol price cut while C-heavy price unrevised. Company capacity about 15-16 crore litres, roughly 50% molasses and 50% grain.
Bioseed Kharif hit by El Nino; corn, cotton and paddy acreage below last year, cotton volumes better YoY.

qa_highlights.question: What is the breakup of the chemicals margin decline on a YoY basis?
qa_highlights.answer: Amit Agarwal said production costs rose about 6-8% across chemistries while selling prices fell about 4-6%, with coal-linked power the key driver for caustic; hydrogen peroxide was the only product that improved.

qa_highlights.question: What is the current PVC price and demand outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Current PVC prices are Rs 95,000-1 lakh per tonne. Demand expected to pick up in Q3 and Q4 post-monsoon; company running at or above 100% of capacity.

qa_highlights.question: Is there risk of Chinese PVC dumping?
qa_highlights.answer: Ajay Shriram said the MIP of USD 766 plus import duty should keep prices stable.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the demerger?
qa_highlights.answer: Amit Agarwal said the process is at an advanced stage and the company is targeting board approval soon, with Q1 FY28 as the target timeline.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for Vinyl margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Amit Agarwal said margins improved YoY and QoQ, but future margins depend on energy prices, which are about 60-70% of PVC cost; renewable additions at Kota are expected to help.

qa_highlights.question: What is Sugar crushing and recovery outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Crushing starts first week of November at some mills; cane availability lower due to drought, and UP lodging after September rains may hit volumes. Too early to quantify recovery.

qa_highlights.question: What are the chlorine captive and pipeline levels, and is caustic capacity addition a concern?
qa_highlights.answer: Captive consumption expected at 45% (Bharuch) and 62% (Kota); with pipeline customers about 70%. Aditya Shriram said new capacities should be absorbed over the medium to long term, with new chlor-alkali players integrating chlorine into PVC.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Rs 20,000 crore FY28 consolidated turnover target achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Amit Agarwal said the company avoids forward-looking numbers; it has invested about Rs 4,500 crore over 3-4 years and more investment is planned.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Bioseed inventory and provisioning impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Philippines inventory write-off about Rs 12 crore for H1; India provisions about Rs 7-8 crore on government-related receivables, which management expects to recover.

risks_watch: Chemicals margin squeeze: production costs up about 6-8% across chemistries (coal-linked power for caustic) while selling prices fell about 4-6%; management said margins would fall further if prices stay at current levels.
Vinyl margin sustainability: energy is about 60-70% of PVC cost, so margins depend on energy prices; MIP of USD 766/MT plus import duty is the key price support against Chinese dumping.
Sugar crush volumes and recovery: cane availability expected lower from drought in Maharashtra and Karnataka; UP lodging after September rains; visibility only in 2-3 months.

Caustic/chlor-alkali supply: management flagged new caustic capacity and possible near-term supply-demand imbalance; chlorine realisations still negative (about negative Rs 5,000 in Q2, lower again after).

Bioseed and Agri-inputs: weak Kharif acreage, provisions for doubtful debts in India (Rs 7-8 crore) and Philippines write-off (about Rs 12 crore in H1); Shriram Farm Solutions topline timing may reverse in Q3 FY27 subject to crop conditions; urea subsidy requirement could reach Rs 1.2 lakh crore vs Rs 85,000 crore budget.
Demerger timing: board-level scheme targeted soon with implementation around Q1 FY28; management said it wants to avoid a scheme needing later modifications.
key_quotes: So effectively, the margins have got impacted all across except one or two smaller products, but for larger products, it has got impacted.

Going forward, it is difficult to say, although we are hopeful on the prices being firm, as we mentioned in the Chairman's speech as well, that there is minimum import price, which should keep the business healthy.
We generally avoid giving forward-looking statements.
So, we hope to, you know, get it to the Board very soon.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on long-term India demand, capacity commissioning and renewable investments, but cautious on near-term margins, citing input costs, energy prices and agri-input weakness. It was evasive on forward numbers, declining to give the Rs 20,000 crore FY28 turnover target and not commenting on competitor chlorine strategies.

growth.why: No explicit company-wide revenue growth guidance; management points to demand recovery in PVC in Q3-Q4, Shriram Farm timing reversal in Q3, sugar crushing with lower cane availability, and new capacity (Kota solar, Bharuch hybrid, Fenesta extrusion) with utilisation at 89%, but gives no consolidated growth number.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Vinyl PBDIT rose to Rs 51 crore from Rs 12 crore (21.9% margin) and PVC demand should improve post-monsoon with prices at Rs 95,000-1 lakh per tonne, but chemicals margins are squeezed and energy is 60-70% of PVC cost.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Bharuch 58 MW hybrid is on schedule (Q1 FY27 timing), Fenesta Kota extrusion phase two in installation, Calcium Chloride at 133 of 266 TPD still ramping, and 40 MW Kota solar (Rs 145 crore) approved, with utilisation at 89%.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: PVC volumes rose 29% and carbide 15% with the company running at or above 100% capacity, Shriram Farm timing shortfall may reverse in Q3, and PVC demand is expected to improve post-monsoon.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation at 89% (caustic 88% vs 79-80% a year ago) with debottlenecking and caustic increase (Rs 120 crore) and Shriram Teknor lines (Rs 133 crore) already approved, and management says about Rs 4,500 crore invested with pipeline still available.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No revenue or margin raise was given, the FY28 Rs 20,000 crore turnover figure was declined, and near-term margins are under pressure from input costs and energy.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Chemicals PBDIT fell to Rs 158 crore from Rs 254 crore as costs rose 6-8% while prices fell 4-6%, and management said margins would fall further at current prices; Bioseed posted a Rs 41 crore loss.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Fenesta wooden doors facility is on schedule and Calcium Chloride is ramping, but no dated new product launch was specified.

rows.label: Demerger targeted for Q1 FY28
rows.why: Management says the process is at an advanced stage with a board scheme targeted soon and implementation around Q1 FY28, though it wants to avoid later modifications.

rows.label: Renewable power share to one-third
rows.why: Target is about one-third of power from renewables within a year, with 70-80 MW more planned and returns above 20-25%, after 68 MW Kota commissioned and 58 MW Bharuch on schedule.

rows.label: Net debt rising
rows.why: Net debt rose to Rs 917 crore from Rs 773 crore YoY while capex continues and the interim dividend of Rs 62.38 crore is paid, with ROCE down to 12% from 15%.

tone.note: Management was confident on long-term demand, capacity commissioning, renewables and the demerger, but cautious on near-term chemicals and Bioseed margins and declined to give the FY28 turnover target; analysts pressed on chemicals margin breakup, caustic supply and Vinyl sustainability.
